newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Popocatepetl volcano spews out more ash.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Popocatepetl volcano spews out more ash.

text.p: Mexico's giant Popocatepetl volcano blew out a cloud of ash and vapour, its second sign of intense activity this week, state news agency Notimex reported on Wednesday.

In a brief dispatch it said the explosion occured at 10:40 pm/11:40 EDT (0340 GMT) on Tuesday and that emergency officials were immediately sent to towns surrounding the volcano to assess the situation.

On Sunday, the 17,887-foot (5,465 meter) volcano, the sixth tallest in North America, blew a giant canopy of hot ash across hundreds of miles of eastern Mexico, scattering the city of Puebla, one of Mexico's largest cities.
Residents near the volcano were put on alert in case they needed to be evacuated, and aircraft were banned from flying near the crater.

Vulcanologists have played down risks of a major eruption, saying Popocatepetl remained fundamentally stable, and was simply letting off "puffs" of gases and magma, or lava, that build up inside the mountain.
